problems.title: Arithmetic with negative fractional divisors
problems.question: Evaluate $(6.3:(-9/20)-2.6:(-1/20))(-4/19)-0.6:(-0.36)$.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.
steps: The first two quotients are−14 and−52, so their difference is 38.
38·(−4/19)=−8. The final quotient is−5/3.
Thus the result is−8−(−5/3).

problems.title: A final digit with a seventh power
problems.question: Find the last digit of 1237⁷+398·236−19³.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1.
steps: Exponent 7 gives last digit 3. The product 398·236 ends 8, and 19³ ends 9.
The final digit is 3+8−9=2.

problems.title: A disguised squared difference
problems.question: Solve(4a²+3)²+(7−4a²)²−2(4a²+3)(4a²−7)=a+96.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Let U=4a²+3, V=4a²−7. The left side is(U−V)².
steps: U−V=10, so the left side is 100 for every a.

problems.title: A sum of squares equal to zero
problems.question: For which x, y does x²+y²+8x−10y+41=0? Find x+y.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Complete squares:(x+4)²+(y−5)²=0.
steps: Both squares must vanish, so x=−4, y=5.

problems.title: The first clock-hand overlap after 9:00
problems.question: How many minutes after 9:00 do the clock hands first coincide?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: The hour hand starts 270° ahead and moves 0.5° per minute;the minute hand moves 6°.
steps: Relative speed=5.5°/min.
Time=270/5.5=540/11 minutes.

problems.title: An odd number of alternating signs
problems.question: Evaluate(−1)+(−1)²+⋯+(−1)¹⁰¹.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Consecutive terms−1, +1 cancel in pairs.
steps: The first 100 terms cancel;the 101 st equals−1.

problems.title: An equation in powers of two
problems.question: Find natural x satisfying 2^(3x−1)·16/4ˣ=64.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Write 16=2⁴, 4ˣ=2²ˣ, 64=2⁶.
steps: The left side is 2^(3x−1+4−2x)=2^(x+3).
Equate exponents:x+3=6.

problems.title: Even polynomials
problems.question: Which listed polynomials stay unchanged when x is replaced by−x?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: A polynomial is even exactly when all its nonzero powers are even.
steps: 1+x²+x⁴, x⁸+x², and x¹²−1 satisfy this.
The terms−x³ and 2x make the other two change.

problems.title: A square root with two signs
problems.question: 111111−222=a². Find a.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: The left side is 110889=333².
steps: Thus a=333 or−333.
Among the positive choices, 333 is the matching value.
problems.note: The equation alone does not specify a≥0, so the negative solution also exists.

problems.title: Old price as a percentage of the new one
problems.question: A fabric price increases 12%. What percentage of the new price is the original?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: New price=1.12·old, so old/new=1/1.12=25/28.
steps: As a percentage, this is(25/28)·100%=625/7%.

problems.title: Fill a half-full tank with a drain open
problems.question: A tap fills a tank in 4 hours and a drain empties it in 6. How long to fill a half-full tank with both open?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Net rate=1/4−1/6=1/12 tank per hour.
steps: The missing volume is 1/2 tank.

problems.title: Dry mushrooms retain their solids
problems.question: Fresh mushrooms contain 92% water;dried mushrooms 20%. How much dried product comes from 20 kg fresh?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Dry solids remain 20·.08=1.6 kg.
steps: The dried product is 80% solids, so total dried mass=1.6/.8.

problems.title: Recover two work rates
problems.question: Two workers together finish a job in 6 days. At half the first rate and triple the second rate, they finish in 4. How long does the first take for one fifth of the job?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Let rates u, v. Then u+v=1/6, u/2+3v=1/4.
steps: Substituting v=1/6−u gives u/2+1/2−3u=1/4, so u=1/10.
One fifth of a job takes(1/5)/(1/10).

problems.title: Factor decimal squares
problems.question: Evaluate(2.16²−4.32·0.84+0.84²)/(2.16²−0.84²).
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: The numerator is(2.16−0.84)²;denominator=(2.16−0.84)(2.16+0.84).
steps: Cancel the nonzero common factor, giving 1.32/3.

problems.title: A minimum gives a linear combination
problems.question: At(x₁, y₁), (2x+3y+5)²+(x−4y−25)⁴−3 is least. Find 4x₁+6y₁.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Both nonnegative powers can vanish simultaneously.
steps: Solving 2x+3y+5=0 and x−4y−25=0 gives x=5, y=−5.
The minimum is−3. In particular, 2x₁+3y₁=−5, so twice that expression is−10.

problems.title: Choose the smaller angle between two rays
problems.question: AOC=89.7°, COD=90.5°, and A, D lie on opposite sides of line OC. Find AOD.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: The angle passing through OC is 89.7°+90.5°=180.2°.
steps: The smaller angle is its complement to 360°.

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector through a triangle vertex
problems.question: A line through A perpendicularly bisects median BD. Find AB:AC.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: A lies on the perpendicular bisector of BD, so AB=AD.
steps: D is midpoint of AC, because BD is a median. Hence AD=AC/2.

problems.title: Consecutive integer sides and perpendicular special lines
problems.question: A triangle has three consecutive natural side lengths. A median is perpendicular to an angle bisector. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: A median and an internal bisector from different vertices being perpendicular forces one of their adjacent triangle sides to be twice another.
steps: To see this, reflect the median vertex A across bisector BD. Its image lies on BC and on the perpendicular median line AM, so it is midpoint M of BC. Thus AB=BM=BC/2.
Among consecutive lengths n, n+1, n+2, a2:1 pair gives n=1 or 2. The first gives degenerate 1, 2, 3. The second gives 2, 3, 4, which is a triangle.
The 2:1 relation also produces the required perpendicular median and bisector in that triangle.

problems.title: Which diagrams show parallel lines?
problems.question: Among the four source diagrams, which have m∥n?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Parallel transversals have equal alternate angles or supplementary same-side angles.
steps: Diagram 1 has 128°+52°=180°, so its lines are parallel. Diagram 3 has equal alternate exterior angles 26°.
Diagram 2 has 103°+76°=179°, and diagram 4 has unequal 159°, 156°;these fail.

problems.title: Distance between two segment midpoints
problems.question: On AC, B satisfies BC=2 AB. D∈BC with BD:DC=3:7, and DC−BD=16 cm. Find the distance between midpoints of AB and CD.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Write BD=3t, DC=7t, so 4t=16 and t=4.
steps: The midpoints are 10 and 46.

problems.title: An angle bisector in a30-60-90 triangle
problems.question: In MKE, K=90°, E=30°, KE=12 cm. Find bisector MC, with C∈KE.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: MK=4√3, ME=8√3 by the 30-60-90 side ratios.
steps: The angle-bisector theorem gives KC:CE=MK:ME=1:2, so KC=4.
Triangle MKC is right, and MC=√[(4√3)²+4²]=√64.

problems.title: Centers of equal-radius circles through a point
problems.question: What is the locus of centers of radius-R circles passing through fixed point A?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: A circle with center O passes through A exactly when OA=R.
steps: All points distance R from A form a circle centered at A.
problems.answer: A circle of radius R centered at A, for R>0.

problems.title: A parallelogram bisector cuts its opposite side
problems.question: In the source BC∥AD, AB=3 cm, BC=10 cm, and the BAD bisector meets BC at K. Find KC.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Because BK∥AD, angle BKA=KAD=BAK.
steps: Triangle ABK is isosceles, so BK=AB=3.
KC=BC−BK=10−3.

problems.title: Two successive perpendicular projections
problems.question: A, D lie on one side of angle B;C, E on the other. AC⊥BC, DE⊥BC, CD⊥AB, B=30°, AC=12 cm. Find DE.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: In right ABC, BC=AC/tan 30°=12√3.
steps: D is the perpendicular projection of C onto AB, so BD=BCcos 30°=18.
E projects D onto BC, so DE=BDsin 30°=9.

problems.title: An exterior bisector and two angle sums
problems.question: In the source BD=DC, DN⊥BC, and DM bisects BDA. Find MBN+BMD.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and verify the original conditions.
formulas: Let angle DBC=DCB=γ and full angle ABC=β.
steps: BDC=180°−2γ, so adjacent BDA=2γ. Its bisector gives BDM=γ.
MBD=β−γ, therefore BMD=180°−(β−γ)−γ=180°−β.
Since BN lies along BC, MBN=β. Add the two.
